newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: EU seen releasing funds soon for Portuguese dam.
newsitem.headline: EU seen releasing funds soon for Portuguese dam.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to release at least 50 billion escudos ($293 million) soon for the construction of a dam in southeast Portugal, a senior Portuguese official said.

The 100 billion escudo ($586 million) dam being built in the parched Alentejo region depends on Portuguese and European Union (EU) financing, said Aderito Vicente Serrao, head of EDIA, the state company overseeing the project.

"I believe the European Commission will release at least 50 billion escudos of regional development, structural and cohesion funds very soon, certainly this year, covering the period to 1999," he told Reuters in an interview on Monday.

He said that last month EU Regional Policy Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies had received a letter from the Spanish government confirming its backing for the dam at Alqueva, which will use water from the River Guadiana flowing from Spain.
"This commitment brings us a step closer to receiving the funds," Serrao said.

The dam, which will have the biggest capacity in Europe encompassing 4,150 million cubic metres, will provide a strategic reserve of water for the Alentejo, whose cereal and wine farmers have been hit by desertification of their land.
"The dam will enable water to be distributed more efficiently in a region often hit by drought," Serrao said.

A joint Portuguese-Spanish consortium, including Portuguese companies Somague and Bento Pedroso, a unit of Edifer, and Spanish companies Dragados and Cubiertas were building the dam, due to open in 2001.
The project will create additional jobs, in construction and tourism, and boost the local economy, one of the EU's less developed areas hit by an exodus of labour to the cities in recent years.
Serrao said public competitions for concessions to build the dam's irrigation system would be launched in the coming months. Foreign bidders in partnership with Portuguese companies would be welcome.

A 30 billion escudo ($175 million) 240 MW hydroelectric power station being built near the dam would serve the national grid when it starts operations in 2001 and could be used to export electricity if required, Serrao said.
